subject: math
title: Classify Two-Dimensional Figures: Triangles, Quadrilaterals and the Hierarchy of Shapes
seo_title: Grade 5 Classifying 2D Shapes Worksheets: Quadrilateral Hierarchy, Types of Triangles (5.G.B.3-4)
standard_text: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category. For example, all rectangles have four right angles and squares are rectangles, so all squares have four right angles. Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 worksheets on classifying 2D figures: equilateral, isosceles and scalene triangles, acute, right and obtuse triangles, parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses, squares and trapezoids, the quadrilateral hierarchy diagram, and always/sometimes/never. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: A smaller group keeps every property of the bigger group it belongs to.
key_sub: All rectangles have 4 right angles, and squares are rectangles, so all squares have 4 right angles. Properties pass down the hierarchy, never up: a square is a rectangle and a rhombus, but not every rectangle is a square.
body_html:
The big idea: a smaller group keeps every property

Shapes are sorted into groups by their properties (sides and angles). A subcategory is a smaller group inside a bigger one. Every shape in the smaller group has all the properties of the bigger group, plus more.

All rectangles have 4 right angles. Squares are rectangles. So all squares have 4 right angles. Properties pass down to the smaller group, never up: squares have 4 equal sides, but most rectangles do not.

Classify triangles

Name a triangle two ways: by its sides and by its angles. Tick marks show equal sides, and a small square shows a right angle.

By sidesMeaningBy anglesMeaning
Equilateral3 equal sidesAcute3 acute angles
Isoscelesat least 2 equal sidesRight1 right angle
Scaleneno equal sidesObtuse1 obtuse angle

An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides, so it is also isosceles. Use both names for the full name: a right angle and 2 equal sides make a right isosceles triangle. A triangle can never be right and obtuse at the same time.

Classify quadrilaterals

Arrows show parallel sides. Shapes with 2 pairs of arrows are parallelograms; a trapezoid has 1 pair.

ShapeWhat it must haveIt is also a
Parallelogram2 pairs of parallel sidesquadrilateral
Rectanglea parallelogram with 4 right anglesparallelogram
Rhombusa parallelogram with 4 equal sidesparallelogram
Square4 right angles and 4 equal sidesrectangle, rhombus, parallelogram
Trapezoidexactly 1 pair of parallel sides (in this unit)quadrilateral
Kite2 pairs of equal sides next to each otherquadrilateral

Some books define a trapezoid as a quadrilateral with at least 1 pair of parallel sides, so a parallelogram is a trapezoid there. Every trapezoid in this unit has exactly 1 pair, so both definitions agree.

The hierarchy

A hierarchy diagram shows which groups are inside which. A line going down (or a box inside a box) means "is a kind of".

Example

All parallelograms have opposite sides that are equal. Is this true for every rhombus?

A rhombus is a parallelogram, so it gets every property of a parallelogram.

Answer: yes

Example

A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. Which names fit?

4 equal sides: rhombus. 4 right angles: rectangle. Both are parallelograms and quadrilaterals. Square tells the most.

Answer: square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, quadrilateral

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
A square is not a rectangleA rectangle needs only 4 right angles. Every square is a rectangle
A rhombus must look like a diamondA rhombus needs only 4 equal sides. A square sitting flat is a rhombus
All rectangles are squaresOnly rectangles with 4 equal sides are squares
An equilateral triangle is not isoscelesIsosceles means at least 2 equal sides, and 3 is at least 2
A right triangle can also be obtuseA triangle has at most 1 angle of 90° or more
Properties pass up the hierarchyOnly down: a square has every property of a rectangle, not the other way

faq.a: Yes. A rhombus is a parallelogram with 4 equal sides, and every square has 4 equal sides. A square is a rhombus that also has 4 right angles.
Yes. A rectangle has 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram with 4 right angles. Not every parallelogram is a rectangle.

faq.q: Is an equilateral triangle also isosceles?
faq.a: Yes, when isosceles means at least 2 equal sides, which is the definition most math programs use. An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides.

It depends on the book. If a trapezoid has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides, a parallelogram is not a trapezoid; if it has at least 1 pair, every parallelogram is a trapezoid. Check which definition your class uses.

sets.title: Classify triangles by sides and angles

items.q: A triangle has sides of 6 in, 6 in and 6 in. Which names fit it?
items.e: All 3 sides are equal, so it is equilateral. It has at least 2 equal sides, so it is also isosceles.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, so it is a right triangle. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is right scalene triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its name.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: One angle is wider than a right angle, so it is obtuse. The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. Its full name is obtuse isosceles triangle. Having 2 acute angles does not make it acute: look at the largest angle.

items.q: Which triangle is scalene?
items.e: Triangle D has no equal sides, so it is scalene. The others have tick marks on at least 2 sides, so they are isosceles (one is also equilateral).

items.q: Can a right triangle also be an obtuse triangle?
c: No, only 1 angle can be 90° or more
items.e: A right angle and an obtuse angle together are already more than 180°, the total of a triangle's angles. So a triangle has at most 1 angle that is 90° or more.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: All 3 angles are smaller than a right angle, so it is acute. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is acute scalene triangle.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, so it is a right triangle. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is right scalene triangle.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. Classify it by its sides.
items.e: 2 sides are 5 cm, so it has 2 equal sides. That makes it isosceles.

items.q: Can a right triangle be isosceles?
items.e: A right isosceles triangle has a right angle and 2 equal sides, like half of a square cut corner to corner.

items.q: A triangle has angles of 100°, 40° and 40°. Classify it by its angles.
items.e: 100° is more than 90°, so it is an obtuse triangle. Every triangle has at least 2 acute angles, so name it by its largest angle.

items.q: A triangle has three 60° angles. Classify it by its angles.
items.e: 60° is less than 90°, so all 3 angles are acute: it is an acute triangle. (Equilateral is a name by sides, not by angles.)

items.q: Which names fit this triangle?
items.e: The tick marks show 3 equal sides, so it is equilateral. An isosceles triangle has at least 2 equal sides, and this one has 3, so it is isosceles too.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. The third side has no tick mark, so it is not equilateral. (Obtuse describes an angle, and this triangle has no obtuse angle.)

items.q: Which is a right isosceles triangle?
items.e: Triangle A has a right angle (the small square) and 2 equal sides (the tick marks). The other right triangle is scalene, and the other isosceles triangles are acute and obtuse.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, so it is a right triangle. The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. Its full name is right isosceles triangle. The other 2 angles are acute, but a triangle is named by its largest angle.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: All 3 angles are smaller than a right angle, so it is acute. The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. Its full name is acute isosceles triangle. Only 2 sides have tick marks, so it is not equilateral. Standing on its point does not change its name.

items.q: A roof frame is a triangle. Its two slanted sides are each 12 feet long, and the bottom is 20 feet long. The top angle is obtuse. What is the full name of the triangle?
items.e: The top angle is obtuse, so it is an obtuse triangle. The two 12-foot sides are equal, so it is isosceles.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 4 m, 7 m and 9 m. Classify it by its sides.
items.e: All 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: One angle is wider than a right angle, so it is obtuse. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is obtuse scalene triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its name.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides.
items.e: There are no tick marks and the 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. (Right describes an angle, and this triangle has no right angle.)

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does every parallelogram have?
items.e: A parallelogram has 2 pairs of parallel sides: each side is parallel to the side across from it. (4 is the number of sides.)

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezoid, not a parallelogram.

items.q: Which shape is a parallelogram but not a rectangle?
items.e: Shape C has 2 pairs of parallel sides and no right angles. The rectangle and the square have 4 right angles, and the trapezoid has only 1 pair of parallel sides.

items.q: Which name does NOT fit this shape?
items.e: It has 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus, a parallelogram and a quadrilateral. It has no right angles, so it is not a rectangle.

items.q: Which names fit this shape?
items.e: 4 right angles make it a rectangle. 4 equal sides make it a rhombus. Both together make it a square, so all three names fit.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezoid, not a parallelogram. It has 2 right angles, but a rectangle needs 4.

items.q: Which name does NOT fit this shape?
items.e: It has 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram, a quadrilateral and a polygon. It has no right angles, so it is not a rectangle.

items.q: What must every rectangle have?
items.e: A rectangle is a parallelogram with 4 right angles. Its sides may all be equal: then it is a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. It has no right angles (not a rectangle) and its sides are not all equal (not a rhombus).

items.q: A tabletop has 4 right angles. It is 6 feet long and 3 feet wide. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 right angles make a rectangle. The sides are not all equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides next to each other, so it is a kite. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus, and it has no parallel sides.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. It has no right angles, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. Only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square. It is also a parallelogram, but rectangle tells more.

items.q: What must every rhombus have?
items.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram with 4 equal sides. It does not need right angles, and it can be turned any way.

items.q: Which name does NOT fit this shape?
items.e: It has 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle, a parallelogram and a quadrilateral. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. It has no right angles, so it is not a square. Standing it on a point does not change its name.

items.q: Which shape has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides?
items.e: Shape B is a trapezoid: only its top and bottom are parallel. The parallelogram and the rhombus have 2 pairs, and the kite has none.

items.q: A floor tile has 4 equal sides. None of its angles are right angles. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make a rhombus. With no right angles, it is not a square.

items.q: Which shape is a rhombus but not a square?
items.e: Shape D has 4 equal sides but no right angles. The two squares are rhombuses too, but they are squares, and the rectangle is not a rhombus.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides and the small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a square. It is also a rhombus, a rectangle and a parallelogram, but square tells the most. Turning it on a corner does not make it a different shape.

sets.title: The hierarchy diagram: where does each shape belong?

items.q: A kite has 2 short equal sides, 2 long equal sides, and no parallel sides. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is a quadrilateral but not a parallelogram, so it goes in region 1, outside the Parallelograms box. A kite like this has no parallel sides at all.

items.q: A shape is in the Rhombuses group. Which groups must it also be in?
items.e: Follow the lines up from Rhombuses: Parallelograms, then Quadrilaterals. A rhombus is a square only if it has 4 right angles.

items.q: Which statement does the diagram show?
items.e: Rhombuses is below Parallelograms, so every rhombus is a parallelogram. The other statements go the wrong way or across.

items.q: In this diagram, an isosceles triangle has at least 2 equal sides. Which statement is true?
items.e: Equilateral is below Isosceles: 3 equal sides means at least 2 equal sides. Not every isosceles triangle has 3 equal sides.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 2 pairs of parallel sides, no right angles, and sides of 9 cm, 5 cm, 9 cm and 5 cm. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is a parallelogram, but it has no right angles and its sides are not all equal. So it is not a rectangle or a rhombus: region 2.

items.q: Which group in the diagram contains all the others?
items.e: Quadrilaterals is at the top. Every shape below it has 4 sides, so every shape in the diagram is a quadrilateral.

items.q: A square is turned so that it stands on one corner. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is both a rectangle and a rhombus, so it goes where the two boxes overlap: region 5, the squares. Turning does not change its sides or angles, so it is still a square.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 5 cm and 7 cm. Which groups in the diagram does it belong to?
items.e: It has exactly 2 equal sides, so it is in Isosceles, and that is inside Triangles. It is not equilateral.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and no right angles. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is a rhombus but not a rectangle (no right angles), so it goes in region 4.

items.q: Regions 3 and 5 together make up which group?
items.e: The Rectangles box covers region 3 and region 5. So every square (region 5) is a rectangle.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 right angles. Its sides are 8 cm, 3 cm, 8 cm and 3 cm. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is a rectangle but not a rhombus (its sides are not all equal), so it goes in region 3.

items.q: Which region holds the shapes that are both rectangles and rhombuses?
items.e: Region 5 is where the Rectangles box and the Rhombuses box overlap. These shapes have 4 right angles and 4 equal sides: they are the squares.

items.q: Regions 4 and 5 together make up which group?
items.e: The Rhombuses box covers region 4 and region 5. So every square (region 5) is a rhombus.

items.q: Why is there no line between Scalene and Isosceles?
items.e: A scalene triangle has no equal sides and an isosceles triangle has at least 2. A triangle cannot be both.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is both a rectangle and a rhombus, so it goes where the two boxes overlap: region 5, the squares. A square belongs to every box: rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms and quadrilaterals.

items.q: A shape is in the Parallelograms group. Must it also be in the Rectangles group?
items.e: Properties pass down, not up. A parallelogram is a rectangle only if it has 4 right angles.

items.q: A quadrilateral has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is a quadrilateral but not a parallelogram, so it goes in region 1, outside the Parallelograms box. With only 1 pair of parallel sides it is a trapezoid, not a parallelogram.

items.q: Kai draws a shape that belongs in region 5. Which names fit his shape?
items.e: Region 5 is inside all 4 boxes. The shape is a square, a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram and a quadrilateral.

items.q: Squares are below both Rectangles and Rhombuses in the diagram. What does this show?
items.e: Each line going down leads to a smaller group inside the group above it. Squares are under both, so every square is a rectangle and every square is a rhombus.

items.q: A triangle has 3 sides of 4 cm. Which groups in the diagram does it belong to?
items.e: It is equilateral. Follow the lines up: equilateral triangles are isosceles, and isosceles triangles are triangles.

sets.title: Always, sometimes, never: true or false?

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? A parallelogram is a rectangle.
items.e: Only a parallelogram with 4 right angles is a rectangle. Most parallelograms lean and have no right angles.

items.q: Max says this shape is a rhombus, so it cannot be a square. Is he right?
c: No, it is only a square
items.e: The marks show 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. 4 equal sides make it a rhombus, and with 4 right angles it is also a square. Turning does not change its name.

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? An obtuse triangle is scalene.
items.e: Sides of 4, 5 and 8 make an obtuse scalene triangle, but a triangle with 2 equal sides and a wide top angle is obtuse isosceles.

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? A square is a parallelogram.
items.e: A square is a rectangle, and every rectangle is a parallelogram. The property passes down, so a square has 2 pairs of parallel sides too.

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? A right triangle is obtuse.
items.e: A triangle has only 1 angle that is 90° or more. A right triangle already has its 90° angle, so it can never also have an obtuse angle.

items.q: True or false? All squares are rhombuses.
items.e: A rhombus needs 4 equal sides, and every square has 4 equal sides, even when it sits flat.

items.q: Lily says a triangle can be right or isosceles, but not both. Is she right?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle and the tick marks show 2 equal sides. One name is for angles and one is for sides, so a triangle can have both: right isosceles.

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? A rectangle is a rhombus.
items.e: Only a rectangle with 4 equal sides (a square) is a rhombus. A 6 cm by 3 cm rectangle is not a rhombus.

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? A right triangle is isosceles.
items.e: Half of a square cut corner to corner is a right isosceles triangle. A right triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 is scalene.

items.q: True or false? All rectangles are squares.
items.e: Only rectangles with 4 equal sides are squares. A 6 cm by 3 cm rectangle is not a square.

items.q: True or false? All right triangles are scalene.
items.e: A right triangle can have 2 equal sides: that is a right isosceles triangle.

items.q: True or false? All parallelograms are rhombuses.
items.e: Only parallelograms with 4 equal sides are rhombuses. Properties pass down from parallelograms to rhombuses, not up.

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? An isosceles triangle is equilateral.
items.e: Only an isosceles triangle whose third side is also equal is equilateral. Sides of 5, 5 and 8 cm make an isosceles triangle that is not equilateral.

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? An equilateral triangle is isosceles.
items.e: An isosceles triangle has at least 2 equal sides. An equilateral triangle has 3, so it is always isosceles.

items.q: True or false? All squares are rectangles.
items.e: A rectangle needs 4 right angles, and every square has 4 right angles.

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? A rhombus is a parallelogram.
items.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram with 4 equal sides, so every rhombus is a parallelogram.

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? An equilateral triangle is a right triangle.
items.e: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°, so none of them is a right angle.

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? A quadrilateral with exactly 1 pair of parallel sides is a parallelogram.
items.e: A parallelogram needs 2 pairs of parallel sides. A shape with exactly 1 pair is a trapezoid, never a parallelogram.

items.q: Is this true always, sometimes, or never? A scalene triangle is isosceles.
items.e: A scalene triangle has no equal sides, and an isosceles triangle has at least 2. A triangle cannot be both.

items.q: True or false? All isosceles triangles are acute.
items.e: An isosceles triangle can have a right angle or an obtuse angle at the top. Only some isosceles triangles are acute.

sets.title: Properties pass down: clues, mistakes and real-world shapes

items.q: I have 2 pairs of parallel sides and no right angles. My sides are not all equal. What is my best name?
items.e: 2 pairs of parallel sides make a parallelogram. No right angles: not a rectangle. Sides not all equal: not a rhombus.

items.q: All parallelograms have opposite sides that are parallel. Which shapes must have this too?
items.e: Rectangles, rhombuses and squares are all kinds of parallelograms, so the property passes down to all of them.

items.q: I have 4 sides. Two pairs of my sides are equal, and each pair is next to each other. I have no parallel sides. What am I?
items.e: 2 pairs of equal sides next to each other make a kite. With no parallel sides it is not a parallelogram, so it is not a rhombus or a rectangle.

items.q: Omar says, "All parallelograms are rhombuses." Which change makes his statement true?
items.e: Only parallelograms with 4 equal sides are rhombuses. (Every rhombus is a parallelogram, but not the other way around.)

items.q: Nora says, "An equilateral triangle is not isosceles." Which change makes her statement true?
items.e: Isosceles means at least 2 equal sides. An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides, so it is isosceles too.

items.q: I have 4 equal sides, and one of my angles is a right angle. What is my best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make a rhombus. A rhombus is a parallelogram, and when a parallelogram has 1 right angle, all 4 of its angles are right angles. So it is a square.

items.q: I have 3 sides. Two of my sides are equal, and one of my angles is a right angle. What am I?
items.e: A right angle makes it a right triangle, and 2 equal sides make it isosceles.

items.q: Leo says, "A rhombus has to stand on a point like a diamond." Which statement is correct?
c: A rhombus can be turned any way.
A rhombus has no equal sides.
A rhombus must stand on a point.
A rhombus is never a square.
items.e: A rhombus only needs 4 equal sides. Turning it does not change that. A square sitting flat is a rhombus too.

items.q: Maya sorts these shapes into the group "has 4 right angles": a square, a rhombus with no right angles, a rectangle and a trapezoid. Which shapes go in the group?
items.e: Every rectangle has 4 right angles, and a square is a rectangle, so both go in. The rhombus and the trapezoid do not have 4 right angles.

items.q: A tile maker has two bins: one for rectangles and one for rhombuses. A tile has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. Which bin can it go in?
items.e: The tile is a square. 4 right angles make it a rectangle, and 4 equal sides make it a rhombus, so it belongs in both groups.

items.q: All isosceles triangles have at least 2 equal sides. Which triangle must also have at least 2 equal sides?
items.e: Every equilateral triangle is isosceles, so it has at least 2 equal sides (in fact, 3).

items.q: I have 4 sides and 4 right angles. My sides are not all equal. What is my best name?
items.e: 4 right angles make a rectangle. The sides are not all equal, so it is not a square. Rectangle tells more than parallelogram.

items.q: All rectangles have 4 right angles, and all squares are rectangles. What must be true?
items.e: A square is a kind of rectangle, so it gets every property of a rectangle, including 4 right angles.

items.q: A sail is a triangle. One angle is a right angle, and its sides are 3 m, 4 m and 5 m. What is its full name?
items.e: It has a right angle, so it is right. All 3 sides are different, so it is scalene.

items.q: A baseball diamond has 4 sides of 90 feet and 4 right angles. People call it a diamond. Which names fit it?
items.e: 4 equal sides and 4 right angles make a square, so it is also a rectangle and a rhombus. It only looks like a diamond because it is turned.

items.q: Opposite sides of every parallelogram are equal in length. Which shape must also have opposite sides equal?
items.e: A rectangle is a kind of parallelogram, so it has every property of a parallelogram. Trapezoids and kites are not parallelograms.

items.q: A garden bed has 4 sides. The front edge and the back edge are parallel, but the two side edges are not. What is its best name?
items.e: Exactly 1 pair of parallel sides makes a trapezoid. A parallelogram needs 2 pairs.

items.q: All rhombuses have 4 equal sides. Which shape must also have 4 equal sides?
items.e: Every square is a rhombus, so a square gets the 4 equal sides of a rhombus.

items.q: All squares have 4 equal sides. Does that mean all rectangles have 4 equal sides?
c: No, properties pass down, not up
items.e: A square is a special rectangle. What is true for every rectangle is true for squares, but not the other way around.

items.q: Ella says, "All rectangles are squares." Which change makes her statement true?
items.e: A square has 4 right angles, so every square is a rectangle. But most rectangles do not have 4 equal sides.
